dedupe_keys.name: lut bioenergy model spreadsheet data platform of global national sustainable bioenergy potential from residues and wastes to 2050 lut university

description: The LUT-Bioenergy model, by Theophilus Nii Odai Mensah, Ayobami Solomon Oyewo and Christian Breyer of LUT University, is an open spreadsheet tool that estimates sustainable bioenergy potential for every country to 2050 at global and national resolution, and at sub-national level where inputs allow. It counts five residue and waste sources: crop residue, forest residue, livestock manure, humanure and municipal solid waste; energy crops, algae, industrial and aquatic biomass are excluded, the crops for food security and water reasons. The authors describe it as a data platform for energy modellers and policymakers. The Zenodo record holds a global Excel file, zipped files for regions such as Europe, Eurasia, MENA, Sub-Saharan Africa, SAARC, Northeast and Southeast Asia, North and South America, and global workbooks for total, crop residue, forest residue, biogas and municipal waste potential under business-as-usual and towards-sustainability scenarios. It is free under CC BY 4.0, first published in July 2025 and updated in June 2026, and users are asked to cite the Applied Energy article. Coverage is global. Caveats: potentials are modelled, and scope is limited to residues and wastes. Simulation uses are country-level biomass and biogas supply limits for energy system capacity planning. Related records: data-swiss-domestic-biomass-energy-potentials-wsl gives national biomass potentials for Switzerland.
